headline: Lead cut in half —
61 down to 32
body: Second-worst score of the week, with 13 points sat on the bench. Weeks spent building a lead, one weekend giving half of it back.
He signed Lewis-Potter for GW9, got 3 out of him, then binned him for GW10 to sign Mitoma. Who is injured. Still top, though. For now.

headline: Top score of the week —
still picked the wrong keeper
body: 57 points, the best in the league, and Van Hecke played centre-forward from centre-back for 15. Imad's lead is down to 32.
Then there's Verbruggen: 11 points, on the bench. Second week running his backup keeper has outscored his starter. Umar should just start whichever one he likes less.

headline: Benches Awoniyi —
Awoniyi scores nine
body: Rihab finally dropped Awoniyi, and Awoniyi instantly got 9. Gonzalo kept his place and got 2. Nobody in this league reads a striker worse.
Colwill, a GW9 signing, did pay off with 6. Then for GW10 he claimed Branthwaite, the defender Imad had thrown back a week earlier. Rihab shops in other people's bins.

headline: 113 in two weeks —
nobody's hotter
body: 62 last week, 51 this week. No one has scored more over the fortnight, and Vidhun will make sure you know it.
Even his waiver landed: Hill, signed for GW9, scored 6, one of four defenders on 6. Third place is 10 points away and he's stopped pretending to be humble.

headline: Up to fifth —
Welbeck in, Welbeck out
body: McBurnie got 12 and dragged Split the G FC from 7th to 5th. A Hull City striker is currently the best thing about this team.
The waivers tell the real story. For GW9, Flemming out, Welbeck in. Welbeck scored 1. For GW10, Welbeck out, Flemming in. Two players, two claims, back where he started.

headline: Three strikers —
two points each
body: Brobbey, Calvert-Lewin and Delap all scored exactly 2. You couldn't arrange that if you tried. Dulaj didn't try, he just picked them.
Boscagli got 6 on the bench. And Dulaj is the only manager who didn't touch the wire in either window. Either supreme confidence or he's forgotten his password.

headline: Fifth to seventh —
and he funded Sandaru's rebuild
body: 33 points, two places gone. Kavinu and Dulaj both went past him in one weekend.
He dropped Bruno Fernandes to sign McGinn. McGinn scored 0, and a week later Sandaru claimed Fernandes. Truffert, a free agent, got 6, so one move worked. And Cherki got 1. Progress.

headline: Konsa and Ayari: 20 —
everyone else: 15
body: Konsa got 10, Ayari got 10, and the other nine managed 15 between them. The bench, Saka included, got nothing.
For GW9 Ometh re-signed Rayan, a week after dropping him for Ayari. Rayan got 3. Two more claims for GW10 make eight in three weeks. He's not building a squad, he's speed dating.

headline: Zirkzee out —
Emersonn back in
body: In GW8 Samithu dropped Emersonn for Zirkzee. In GW9 he dropped Zirkzee for Emersonn. Emersonn scored 2. Two claims to end up exactly where he started.
The back four scored 25, the front three scored 6. So his GW10 move was to swap one defender for another. Samithu is looking for the leak at the wrong end of the boat.

headline: 26 points —
14 adrift at the bottom
body: Lowest score of the week, and the gap to 9th went from a single point to 14. The bright spot was Robertson, a GW9 signing, with 8.
The other two signings, Mbaye and O'Reilly, got 1 each. Mbaye is already gone for GW10, with Bruno Fernandes and Kluivert coming in. Last place, but he's busy.
